paragraphs: Friend, here's the big idea: Paul's last words in this letter aren't about himself. They're about people. He's in chains, the end is close, and he's still asking for Mark, still greeting Prisca and Aquila, still keeping track of Trophimus, who was left sick in Miletus (2 Timothy 4:11, 19, 20). Ministry was never just a message to Paul. It was people he loved and people he needed.

Some of those people let him down, and I think that stung. Demas left because of his love of this world, and at Paul's first defense, no one stood with him (2 Timothy 4:10, 16). But Paul says, "May it not be charged against them," and he says the Lord stood by him and strengthened him (2 Timothy 4:16, 17). So when people leave you, the Lord is still standing right there, and you can hand the hurt to Him instead of carrying it yourself.

And look at how the letter ends. Paul has a lion's mouth behind him and a heavenly kingdom ahead of him, and he says, "To Him be the glory forever and ever. Amen." (2 Timothy 4:18). His last words are "Grace be with you all." (2 Timothy 4:22). Baker, that's the finish we're baking toward: faithful to the Lord, kind to people, and full of grace.
